### Side-quest: quantify normalized intensities of precursors targeted with SILAC

```{r Quantify number of artifacts with SILAC heavy spike-in}
# Count how many SILAC-[KR]-H spike-ins are in the datasets
d1 <- diann_load(file.path(inDir, "04_ComputationalProteomics", "50-0085_allFiles_Final01_PeptideAtlasWithIS", "report.tsv.bz2"))
d2 <- diann_load(file.path(inDir, "04_ComputationalProteomics", "50-0085_allFiles_Final02_PeptideAtlasWithIS", "report.tsv.bz2"))

df <- as.data.frame(rbind(d1, d2)) %>% dplyr::select(sample_id = File.Name, precursor_id = Precursor.Id, protein_id = Protein.Group, sequence_modified = Modified.Sequence,  sequence_plain = Stripped.Sequence, charge = Precursor.Charge, rt = iRT, intensity = Precursor.Normalised, confidence = Q.Value,  confidence_score = Evidence, gene_symbol = Genes)

df_silac <- df[grep("SILAC-[KR]", df$precursor_id),]
unique(sapply(unique(df_silac$precursor_id), function(s) strsplit(s, "\\(")[[1]][2]))
grep("UniMod", unique(df_silac$precursor_id), value=T)
# Overall, we have 6 variations of the SILAC markers: SILAC-K-H, SILAC-K-L, SILAC-K-decoy, SILAC-R-H, SILAC-R-L, SILAC-R-decoy
# Therefore, in order to get the 
df_silac$precursor_unique_id <- gsub("\\(SILAC-[RK]-decoy\\)", "", gsub("\\(SILAC-[KR]-[LH]\\)", "", df_silac$precursor_id))
df_silac$silac_id <- ifelse(grepl("SILAC-K-decoy", df_silac$precursor_id), "SILAC-K-decoy",
                            ifelse(grepl("SILAC-R-decoy", df_silac$precursor_id), "SILAC-R-decoy",

                                          ifelse(grepl("SILAC-K-H", df_silac$precursor_id), "SILAC-K-H",
                                                 ifelse(grepl("SILAC-R-L", df_silac$precursor_id), "SILAC-R-L",
                                                        ifelse(grepl("SILAC-R-H", df_silac$precursor_id), "SILAC-R-H", NA))))))
mat <- dcast(df_silac, precursor_unique_id+silac_id ~ sample_id, value.var = "intensity")
write.xlsx(mat, file = file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "20250224_SILAC_precursors_intensities.xlsx"))
```

## Merging DIA-NN runs and importing into `msdap` object

Although the samples were measured in two different runs, it was determined they should be run together. Therefore, some samples from the metadata were filtered, and the data from DIA-NN was filtered accordingly:

1.  Cal.QC samples were used as place holders, and could be removed before running the analysis
2.  Samples with "Analysis" column being TRUE were kept
3.  Some samples were repeated because they were outliers in the original run (the repeated samples were marked in the column "OutlierRepeated" as TRUE), and from those samples with repeated "Sample.Name" entries, only those that had OutlierRepeated==TRUE were included

```{r Filter metadata}
df1 <- read.table(file.path(inDir, "04_ComputationalProteomics", "50-0085_allFiles_Final01_PeptideAtlasWithIS", "report.stats.tsv.bz2"))
df2 <- read.table(file.path(inDir, "04_ComputationalProteomics", "50-0085_allFiles_Final02_PeptideAtlasWithIS", "report.stats.tsv.bz2"))

## first, determine which samples from the metadata file are in each dataset
metadata <- read.xlsx(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "01_Metadata", "20250124_AF_50-0085_metadata.xlsx"))
metadata <- metadata[!(metadata$Sample.Type %in% "Cal.QC"),]
metadata_clinical <- read.xlsx(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "01_Metadata", "20250131_AF_50-0085_clinical_metadata.xlsx"))
# Filter for Analysis == TRUE (set exclude for TRUE if Analysis==FALSE)
metadata$exclude <- !metadata$Analysis
metadata <- merge(metadata, metadata_clinical, all=T)
metadata_d1 <- metadata[metadata$sample_id %in% unique(df1$V1),]
metadata_d1$diann_batch <- 1
metadata_d2 <- metadata[metadata$sample_id %in% unique(df2$V1),]
metadata_d2$diann_batch <- 2
# For replicate samples in column "Sample.Name", keep only samples where "OutlierRepeated" is TRUE
metadata_all <- c()
for(i in 1:2){
  obj <- get(paste("metadata_d",i, sep=""))
  dup_samps <- unique(obj$Sample.Name[duplicated(obj$Sample.Name)])
  for(s in dup_samps){
    obj$exclude[obj$Sample.Name %in% s] <- ifelse(obj$OutlierRepeated[obj$Sample.Name %in% s], FALSE, TRUE)
  }
  obj$exclude[is.na(obj$Sample.Name)] <- FALSE
  obj <- obj[!(obj$exclude),]
  metadata_all <- rbind(metadata_all, obj)
  write.xlsx(obj, file = file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "01_Metadata", paste("20250205_AF_50-0085_metadata_Final0", i , "Dataset.xlsx", sep="")))
}
write.xlsx(metadata_all, file = file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "01_Metadata", "20250205_AF_50-0085_metadata_all.xlsx"))
```

With the metadata reduced for samples to be tested, the DIA-NN runs were to be imported, filtered for samples in the metadata file, but also would have peptides containing "SILAC-K-H" and "SILAC-R-H" removed (peptides spiked-in with [heavy SILAC](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28508369/) that had to be removed). The filtered datasets would then be combined and written into a single tsv file that would be later compressed and used in the rest of the workflow.

# Pre-processing

In order to pre-process the data by reducing any issues from technical variability, batch effects and missing values, the following steps need to be done first:

1.  [**Initial QC**]{.underline} - an initial QC value will estimate which samples have too many missing values to be removed before the data is normalized
2.  [**Normalize data**]{.underline} - Vadim Farztdinov recommended `loess` and `modebetween_protein`, where `loess` calls the cyclic loess function `normalizeCyclicLoess` from limma to normalize columns of a matrix (samples) cyclicly to each other on a peptide level, and `modebetween_protein` scales between all pairwise sample groups on a protein level, such that the log-fold-change mode is zero
3.  [**Filter outlier samples and low-presence peptides**]{.underline} - outlier samples based on the QC assessments should be removed, and in case some peptides are expressed in too few samples, they should be removed too
4.  [**Data imputation**]{.underline} - it would be useful to increase as many peptide intensities as possible
5.  [**Batch correction**]{.underline} - there are 8 batches in the entire dataset, with a total of 30 plates used for biological samples, so a batch correction will probably be necessary

## Initial filtration

### Peptide filtration

Furthermore, some peptides should be considered for removal:

1.  [**Non-proteotypic peptides**]{.underline} - peptides mapping to multiple proteins

2.  [**Non-tryptic peptides**]{.underline} - "A trypsin digest is used to cleave the proteins in a sample downstream to every K (lysine) or R (arginine), except when followed by P (proline). The individual components that result after the cleavage step are called tryptic peptides" (<https://unipept.ugent.be/clidocs/casestudies/tpa>). The problem with non-tryptic peptides is that they are not well balanced in terms of their expressions in different peptides, which causes summarisation of peptide expressions into proteins to be unbalanced and unreliable, and therefore should be removed.

```{r identification of non-proteotypic and non-tryptic peptides}
# Remove commercial samples
numAllPrecs <- length(unique(dataset_orig$peptides$peptide_id))
numAllPeps <- length(unique(dataset_orig$peptides$sequence_plain))
numAllProts <- length(unique(dataset_orig$peptides$protein_id))

# Determine how many proteins are tryptic and/or proteotypic
proteotypic <- unique(dataset_orig$peptides$sequence_plain[!grepl(";", dataset_orig$peptides$protein_id)])
tryptic_peps <- read.table("C:/Users/orsh10/Downloads/Annotations/20240605_Human_PeptideAtlas-TrypticPeptides.tsv", header = T)
tryptic <- unique(tryptic_peps$peptide[tryptic_peps$tryptic])
print(ggVennDiagram::ggVennDiagram(list(dataset = unique(dataset_orig$peptides$sequence_plain), tryptic = tryptic[tryptic %in% unique(dataset_orig$peptides$sequence_plain)], proteotypic = proteotypic)) + labs(title = "All, tryptic and proteotipic peptides"))

# Remove non-tryptic peptides
dataset <- remove_exclude_peps(dataset_orig, unique(dataset_orig$peptides$peptide_id[!(dataset_orig$peptides$sequence_plain %in% tryptic)]))
# Set character vectors for batches and plates
dataset$samples$ms_batch <- paste("b", dataset$samples$ms_batch, sep = "")
dataset$samples$analysis_plate <- paste("P", dataset$samples$analysis_plate, sep = "")
dataset$samples$analysis_plate96 <- paste("P", dataset$samples$analysis_plate96, sep = "")
```

It was noticed that within the different datasets, 64-65% of the original set of peptides are kept as tryptic, where 41-44% of all proteins are also proteotypic (21-23% of the proteins which are tryptic are non-proteotypic). As such, it would be possible to remove the non-tryptic peptides without

### QC

After every pre-processing step, it is necessary to run quality control to observe the changes in proportion of NAs in different samples, as well as peptide intensity distributions. For the quality control, two functions are run:

1.  [**qc_diann_figures**]{.underline} - using the DIA-NN generated statistics, the standardized statistics are plotted for each factor. These figures are recalculated after removing outlier samples (they do not change by normalization, data imputation or batch correction)
2.  [**qc_msdap_figures**]{.underline} - the ms-dap list object is used to calculate proportion of NAs in different samples, intensity distribution, sample correlations and coefficient of variation (CoV)

```{r DIANN and msdap QC - initial, warning=FALSE}
outDir <- file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "1_initial_QC")
dir.create(file.path(outDir, "DIA-NN"), showWarnings = F, recursive = T)
diann_stats_files <- list.files(file.path(inDir, "04_ComputationalProteomics"), pattern = "report.stats.tsv.bz2", recursive = T, full.names = T)
df <- Reduce("rbind", lapply(diann_stats_files, function(file) read.table(file, header = T)))
write.table(df, file = file.path(inDir, "04_ComputationalProteomics", "report_all.stats.tsv"), quote = F, sep = "\t", row.names = F)
metadata <- dataset$samples[, c("sample_id", "ms_batch", "sample_type")]
colnames(metadata) <- c("File.Name", "batch", "type")
diann_stats_factors <- c("Total.Quantity", "MS1.Signal", "MS2.Signal", "FWHM.Scans", "FWHM.RT", "Median.Mass.Acc.MS1", "Median.Mass.Acc.MS1.Corrected", "Median.Mass.Acc.MS2", "Median.Mass.Acc.MS2.Corrected", "Normalisation.Instability", "Median.RT.Prediction.Acc", "Average.Peptide.Length", "Average.Peptide.Charge", "Average.Missed.Tryptic.Cleavages")
qc_diann_initial <- qc_diann_figures(diann_stats_file = file.path(inDir, "04_ComputationalProteomics", "report_all.stats.tsv"), metadata = metadata, factors = diann_stats_factors, outDir = file.path(outDir, "DIA-NN"))

dir.create(file.path(outDir, "msdap"), showWarnings = F, recursive = T)
qc_df_initial <- qc_msdap_figures(dataset = dataset, file.path(outDir, "msdap"), intensity = "intensity", type = "sample_type", batch = "ms_batch")
```

## Filtration of outlier samples and low-presence peptides

### Low-presence peptide removal

Usually, Vadim recommends to use 30% as the cutoff for peptide presence: not too high, not too low. However, this time, I thought it may be a good idea to try and determine the best threshold for peptide cutoff based on the data.

Before filtering for number of peptides, it was necessary to see how the peptide measurements were distributed across samples. Therefore, an empirical cumulative distribution function (eCDF) was plotted based on percentage of measured peptides (non-NAs) in all samples (the proportion of samples they were measured in) to see how many peptides are kept at different cutoffs.

```{r Plot percentages of missing values for peptides}
dataset <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "1_initial_QC", "tryptic.Rdata"))
# Retrieve number of peptides measured in each sample when peptides are filtered based on how present they are in the samples
obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])
mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, col = "intensity")

# Calculate presence of peptides in dataset
pep_presence <- 100*rowSums(!is.na(mat))/ncol(mat)
groups <- data.frame(pep_pres = pep_presence, group = cut(pep_presence, breaks = 10))

ggplotly(ggplot(groups, aes(x = pep_pres)) + stat_ecdf(geom = "step"))
ggplotly(ggplot(groups, aes(x = pep_pres)) + geom_histogram(bins = 20))
```

From what can be seen in the graphs, the histogram shows that there are 6172 peptides with \<5% presence, which is the single largest bin in the histogram compared to peptides with higher presence. Furthermore, the eCDF shows the corresponding quantile at 5% presence is \~46%, meaning that when filtering for peptides with at least 5% presence, we already lose 46% of the peptides in the dataset. Still, even though we lose a lot of data already, it is a necessary to justify using a very low presence threshold by making sure that this does not affect the variation of the peptides too much. This can be done by plotting the CoVs for peptide cut-offs 5% to 30% with gaps of 5%, and seeing how the CoVs differ among them.

```{r low-presence peptide removal}
# Select percentage of missingness to filter the samples for
pepFilt_thresholds <- c(0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3)
overall_stats <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "1_initial_QC", "overall_stats.Rdata"))

cov_table <- data.frame(group = unique(paste(obj$samples$ms_batch, obj$samples$sample_type, sep = "_")))
for (pepFilt in pepFilt_thresholds) {
  # Retrieve number of peptides measured in each sample when peptides are filtered based on how present they are in the samples
  obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])
  mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, col = "intensity")

  # Remove peptides expressed in too few samples
  matFilt <- mat[rowSums(!is.na(mat)) >= ncol(mat) * pepFilt, ]
  obj <- remove_exclude_peps(obj, setdiff(rownames(mat), rownames(matFilt)))

  # Remove dt_pep_group and groups sections in dataset, and set them again
  obj$dt_pep_group <- obj$groups <- NULL
  obj <- cache_filtering_data_noCoV(obj)
  # Normalize data
  cat("Normalising data for peptide threshold", pepFilt, "\n")
  obj <- filter_dataset(
    dataset = obj,
    filter_min_detect = 3, # each peptide must have a good confidence score in at least N samples per group
    filter_min_quant = 3, # similarly, the number of reps where the peptide must have a quantitative value
    by_group = T, all_group = F, by_contrast = F,
    rollup_algorithm = rollup_algorithm, norm_algorithm = c("loess", "modebetween_protein")
  ) # loess calls the cyclic loess function normalizeCyclicLoess from limma (recommended by Vadim), and the modebetween_protein scales between all pairwise sample groups on a protein level, such that the log-fold-change mode is zero
  
  # Set colors for different samples
  obj$samples$cov_col <- paste(obj$samples$ms_batch, obj$samples$sample_type, sep = "_")
  samples_colors_long <- sample_color_coding__long_format(obj$samples)
  samples_colors <- samples_colors_long %>%
    dplyr::select(sample_id, shortname, prop, clr) %>%
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(sample_id, shortname), names_from = prop, values_from = clr)

  # Create coefficient of variation plot
  pep_cov <- ggplot_coefficient_of_variation(tib_input = obj$peptides, samples = obj$samples, samples_colors = samples_colors, column = "cov_col", intensity_norm = TRUE)
  
  tmp <- as.data.frame(pep_cov$data %>% group_by(group) %>% summarise(mean_cov = mean(cov)))
  colnames(tmp) <- c("group", paste("mean_cov_filt", pepFilt, sep="_"))
  cov_table <- merge(cov_table, tmp)
  
  mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, peptide_id ~ sample_id, col = "intensity_by_group")
  peptideNA <- 100 * sum(is.na(mat)) / length(mat)
  
  mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, protein_id ~ sample_id, col = "intensity_by_group")
  proteinNA <- 100 * sum(mat == 0) / length(mat)
  
  overall_stats[[paste("filt_thresh_", pepFilt, sep = "")]] <- c(nrow(obj$samples), length(unique(obj$peptides$peptide_id)), length(unique(obj$peptides$protein_id)), peptideNA, proteinNA)
  overall_stats[[paste("filt_perc_thresh_", pepFilt, sep = "")]] <- 100 * overall_stats[[paste("filt_thresh_", pepFilt, sep = "")]] / overall_stats$orig
  
  print(pep_cov + labs(title = paste("COV peptides filtered %age NA under", pepFilt)))
}
print(overall_stats)

df <- melt(cov_table)
colnames(df) <- c("group", "threshold", "cov")
df$threshold <- as.factor(as.numeric(gsub("mean_cov_filt_", "", df$threshold)))
ggplot(data = df, aes(x=threshold, y=cov, group=group, label=round(cov,2))) + geom_line(color="red") + geom_point() +geom_text(hjust=0, vjust=0) + geom_dl(aes(label=group), method = list(dl.trans(x=x+0.2), "last.points"))
```

The CoV plots should show high CoV for biological samples (high biological variance) and low CoV for MS.QC samples (low technical variance). From the plots for the mean CoVs in each group, we generally see a down trend in biological batches as we go from 5% to 30% thresholds, which would justify using lower threshold, as we prefer more biological variance from a higher CoV. Comparatively, the trend of the MS.QC batches also go down as we increase the threshold, but only by a small amount (1% at most), so it is not worth to lose hundreds of precursors to filtering if the CoV for technical variation is only to only slightly improve. Therefore, the selected threshold for the peptides was 10% presence. However, in the end, the absolute number of precursors and proteins with high presence is more important than the proportion of precursors and proteins being removed, so the 30% presence cutoff was chosen after all.

```{r Filter out peptides measured in less than 30% of the samples}
overall_stats[, grep("filt_", colnames(overall_stats))] <- NULL
obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])
mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, col = "intensity")

# Remove peptides expressed in too few samples
matFilt <- mat[rowSums(!is.na(mat)) >= ncol(mat) * 0.3, ]
dataset <- remove_exclude_peps(dataset, setdiff(rownames(mat), rownames(matFilt)))

# Remove dt_pep_group and groups sections in dataset, and set them again
dataset$dt_pep_group <- dataset$groups <- NULL
dataset <- cache_filtering_data_noCoV(dataset)
# Normalize data
cat("Normalising data\n")
dataset <- filter_dataset(
  dataset = dataset,
  filter_min_detect = 3, # each peptide must have a good confidence score in at least N samples per group
  filter_min_quant = 3, # similarly, the number of reps where the peptide must have a quantitative value
  by_group = T, all_group = F, by_contrast = F,
  rollup_algorithm = rollup_algorithm, norm_algorithm = c("loess", "modebetween_protein")
) # loess calls the cyclic loess function normalizeCyclicLoess from limma (recommended by Vadim), and the modebetween_protein scales between all pairwise sample groups on a protein level, such that the log-fold-change mode is zero

# Create directory for QC results
outDir <- file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "2_filtPeps")
dir.create(outDir, showWarnings = F, recursive = T)
saveRDS(object = dataset, file = file.path(outDir, "filtPep.Rdata"))
```

### Removing outlier samples

After removing the low-presence peptides at the 30% cut-off, it appears that when determining sample outliers based on percentage of NAs, 37% seems to be a good cut-off, so only samples with less than 37% of NAs will be kept

```{r Remove outlier samples}
dataset <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "2_filtPeps", "filtPep.Rdata"))
overall_stats <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "1_initial_QC", "overall_stats.Rdata"))
mat <- dfToMat(dataset$peptides, col = "intensity_by_group")
dataset$samples$percNA <-  sapply(dataset$samples$sample_id, function(s) {
  tmp <- mat[, colnames(mat) %in% s]
  sum(is.na(tmp)) / length(tmp)
  })
dataset$samples$exclude <- ifelse(dataset$samples$percNA < 0.37, FALSE, TRUE)

# Remove dt_pep_group and groups sections in dataset, and set them again
dataset$dt_pep_group <- dataset$groups <- NULL
dataset <- cache_filtering_data_noCoV(dataset)
# Normalize data

dataset <- filter_dataset(
  dataset = dataset,
  filter_min_detect = 3, # each peptide must have a good confidence score in at least N samples per group
  filter_min_quant = 3, # similarly, the number of reps where the peptide must have a quantitative value
  by_group = T, all_group = F, by_contrast = F,
  rollup_algorithm = rollup_algorithm, norm_algorithm = c("loess", "modebetween_protein")
) # loess calls the cyclic loess function normalizeCyclicLoess from limma (recommended by Vadim), and the modebetween_protein scales between all pairwise sample groups on a protein level, such that the log-fold-change mode is zero

obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])

proteinNA <- 100 * sum(mat == 0) / length(mat)

overall_stats$filt_thresh_0.3 <- c(nrow(obj$samples), length(unique(obj$peptides$peptide_id)), length(unique(obj$peptides$protein_id)), peptideNA, proteinNA)
overall_stats$filt_perc_thresh_0.3 <- 100 * overall_stats$filt_thresh_0.3 / overall_stats$orig
```

## Imputation

As suggested by Michael, we want to impute the data little by little. Therefore, the best options for levels of imputation in the data were determined to be: 1. Imputation by plate, allowing 15% missingness 2. Imputation by severeness (biological samples only), allowing for 33% missingness 3. Imputation by sample_type (biological, MS.QC and SP.QC), allowing for 66% missingness 4. Overall imputation if there are any more missing values in the end

Since there are different tools for imputation, chatGPT was asked to suggest the best tools/functions to use at each level. Several methods were considered for the imputation:

| Feature                               | BPCA (`pcaMethods`)                                                       | PPCA (`pcaMethods`)                                 | kNN (`VIM`)                                | PMM (`mice`)                                             |
|--------------|----------------|----------------|--------------|--------------|
| Speed                                 | Fast (Bayesian updates)                                                   | Very Fast (low-rank approx.)                        | Slow (distance-based)                      | Very Slow (iterative, regression-based)                  |
| Scalability                           | Excellent for large data                                                  | Excellent for large data                            | Slows significantly with more samples      | High memory and computation demand                       |
| Captures Biological Structure?        | Yes (PCA-based low-rank structure)                                        | Yes (PCA projection)                                | Yes (local peptide patterns)               | Yes (Predictive modeling maintains data relationships)   |
| Handles Nonlinear Relationships?      | Not well (assumes linear structure)                                       | Not well (Gaussian noise assumption)                | Better at capturing nonlinear patterns     | Yes (regression captures complex relationships)          |
| Missingness Tolerance                 | Works well up to \~50% missingness                                        | Works well up to \~50% missingness                  | Works well up to \~50% missingness         | Handles high missingness if MAR (up to \~60-70%)         |
| Computational Cost                    | Low (matrix factorization-based)                                          | Low (probabilistic approximation)                   | High (pairwise distance calculations)      | High (multiple imputations and iterations)               |
| Assumes Data is Normal/Gaussian?      | Assumes normality                                                         | Assumes normality                                   | No assumption, distance-based              | No assumption, flexible model                            |
| Best for                              | Continuous data with global structure (e.g., proteomics, gene expression) | Continuous data with a probabilistic structure      | Local peptide correlations, small datasets | Complex datasets where relationships should be preserved |
| Not ideal if...                       | Data is highly nonlinear                                                  | Data is nonlinear or non-Gaussian                   | Dataset is too large (slow)                | Too much computational time required                     |
| Recommended for your proteomics data? | Yes (fast, structured imputation, preserves biological trends)            | Yes (even faster, slightly less accurate than BPCA) | No (too slow for large proteomics data)    | No (too computationally expensive)                       |

```{r Load required libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

```{r Define missingness threshold function}
get_missingness <- function(data) {
  rowMeans(is.na(data)) * 100  # Get percentage of missing values per peptide (rows)
}
```

### Level 1: plate-level imputation

For plate-level imputation, Vadim suggested using bpca imputation, as it works well on small-scaled data.

```{r Plate-level imputation (≤25% missingness)}
dataset <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "2_filtSamps", "filtSamps.Rdata"))
overall_stats <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "2_filtSamps", "overall_stats.Rdata"))

dataset$peptides <- as_tibble(merge(dataset$samples[,c("sample_id", "shortname")], dataset$peptides))
obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])
mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, peptide_id ~ shortname, col = "intensity_by_group")

data_imputed <- mat
plates <- unique(obj$samples$analysis_plate96)
plates <- plates[order(as.numeric(gsub("P", "", plates)))]

percNA_trace <- data.frame(level = "orig", percNA = 100 * sum(is.na(data_imputed)) / length(data_imputed))
for (plate in plates) {
  plate_samples <- obj$samples$shortname[obj$samples$analysis_plate96 == plate]
  subset_data <- mat[, colnames(mat) %in% plate_samples]  # Extract data for the plate
  
  missingness <- get_missingness(subset_data)
  peptides_to_impute <- names(missingness[missingness <= 25])

  if (length(peptides_to_impute) > 0) {
    start.time <- Sys.time()
    tmp <- impute.matrix(subset_data[peptides_to_impute, ], method = "bpca")
    end.time <- Sys.time()
    cat("Finished imputing plate", plate,"\n")
    print(end.time - start.time)
    data_imputed[peptides_to_impute, plate_samples] <- as.matrix(tmp[, plate_samples])
  }
  percNA_trace <- as.data.frame(rbind(percNA_trace, c(plate, 100 * sum(is.na(data_imputed)) / length(data_imputed))))
}
df <- melt(data_imputed)
colnames(df) <- c("peptide_id", "shortname", "intensity_by_group_imputed")
dataset$peptides <- merge(dataset$peptides, df, all = T)
dataset$peptides$sample_id <- dataset$samples$sample_id[match(dataset$peptides$shortname, dataset$samples$shortname)]
prot_df <- unique(dataset$peptides[!is.na(dataset$peptides$protein_id), c("peptide_id", "protein_id")])
dataset$peptides$protein_id <- prot_df$protein_id[match(dataset$peptides$peptide_id, prot_df$peptide_id)]
  
# Create directory for QC results
outDir <- file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "3_1_imputedPlate")
dir.create(outDir, showWarnings = F, recursive = T)
saveRDS(object = dataset, file = file.path(outDir, "impute_plate.Rdata"))

obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])
mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, peptide_id ~ sample_id, col = "intensity_by_group_imputed")
peptideNA <- 100 * sum(is.na(mat)) / length(mat)

mat <- rollup_pep2prot(obj$peptides %>% dplyr::select(peptide_id, protein_id, sample_id, intensity = intensity_by_group_imputed), rollup_algorithm = rollup_algorithm, intensity_is_log2 = T, return_as_matrix = T)
proteinNA <- 100 * sum(is.na(mat)) / length(mat)

overall_stats$impute_plate <- c(nrow(obj$samples), length(unique(obj$peptides$peptide_id)), length(unique(obj$peptides$protein_id)), peptideNA, proteinNA)
overall_stats$impute_plate_perc <- 100 * overall_stats$impute_plate / overall_stats$orig
print(overall_stats)
saveRDS(object = overall_stats, file = file.path(outDir, "overall_stats.Rdata"))
```

### Level 2: group-based severity imputation

On the severity level, Vadim suggested using the `knn` method from the `impute` R package, simply because it is best on data with many different samples.

```{r Biological Group Imputation (≤33% missingness)}
dataset <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "3_1_imputedPlate", "impute_plate.Rdata"))
overall_stats <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "3_1_imputedPlate", "overall_stats.Rdata"))

obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])
mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, peptide_id ~ shortname, col = "intensity_by_group_imputed")

data_imputed <- mat
groups <- unique(obj$samples$severe)
groups <- groups[!is.na(groups)]

for (group in groups) {
  group_samples <- obj$samples$shortname[obj$samples$severe == group]
  subset_data <- mat[, colnames(mat) %in% group_samples]  # Extract data for the plate
  
  missingness <- get_missingness(subset_data)
  peptides_to_impute <- names(missingness[missingness <= 33])

  if (length(peptides_to_impute) > 0) {
    start.time <- Sys.time()
    tmp <- impute.matrix(subset_data[peptides_to_impute, ], method = "knn")
    end.time <- Sys.time()
    cat("Finished imputing group", group,"\n")
    print(end.time - start.time)
    data_imputed[match(rownames(tmp), rownames(data_imputed)), match(colnames(tmp), colnames(data_imputed))] <- tmp
  }
  percNA_trace <- as.data.frame(rbind(percNA_trace, c(group, 100 * sum(is.na(data_imputed)) / length(data_imputed))))
}
df <- melt(data_imputed)
colnames(df) <- c("peptide_id", "shortname", "intensity_by_group_imputed")
dataset$peptides$intensity_by_group_imputed <- NULL
dataset$peptides <- merge(dataset$peptides, df, all = T)
dataset$peptides$sample_id <- dataset$samples$sample_id[match(dataset$peptides$shortname, dataset$samples$shortname)]
prot_df <- unique(dataset$peptides[!is.na(dataset$peptides$protein_id), c("peptide_id", "protein_id")])
dataset$peptides$protein_id <- prot_df$protein_id[match(dataset$peptides$peptide_id, prot_df$peptide_id)]
  
# Create directory for QC results
outDir <- file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "3_2_imputedSeverity")
dir.create(outDir, showWarnings = F, recursive = T)
saveRDS(object = dataset, file = file.path(outDir, "impute_severity.Rdata"))

obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])
mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, peptide_id ~ sample_id, col = "intensity_by_group_imputed")
peptideNA <- 100 * sum(is.na(mat)) / length(mat)

mat <- rollup_pep2prot(obj$peptides %>% dplyr::select(peptide_id, protein_id, sample_id, intensity = intensity_by_group_imputed), rollup_algorithm = rollup_algorithm, intensity_is_log2 = T, return_as_matrix = T)
proteinNA <- 100 * sum(is.na(mat)) / length(mat)

overall_stats$impute_severity <- c(nrow(obj$samples), length(unique(obj$peptides$peptide_id)), length(unique(obj$peptides$protein_id)), peptideNA, proteinNA)
overall_stats$impute_severity_perc <- 100 * overall_stats$impute_severity / overall_stats$orig
print(overall_stats)
saveRDS(object = overall_stats, file = file.path(outDir, "overall_stats.Rdata"))
```

```{r msdap QC imputed data - level 2}
cat("Calculating PCA with normalized values using imputation method bpca\n")
obj$samples$ms_batch_n <- as.numeric(gsub("b", "", obj$samples$ms_batch))

obj$samples$analysis_plate96_n <- as.numeric(gsub("P", "", obj$samples$analysis_plate96))

```

### Level 3: global imputation

On the final imputation, Vadim suggested again `kNN` (large dataset). However, before imputing the data and adding it to the dataset, it is a good idea to determine whether it is better to use 34% or 40% missingness as the threshold. For that, it is necessary to compare the CoV plots and the intensity distributions of samples at the different missingness levels.

```{r Assess global imputation (34% or 40% missingness)}
dataset <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "3_2_imputedSeverity", "impute_severity.Rdata"))
overall_stats <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "3_2_imputedSeverity", "overall_stats.Rdata"))

for(miss in c(34, 40)){
  obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])
  mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, peptide_id ~ shortname, col = "intensity_by_group_imputed")
  data_imputed <- mat

  missingness <- get_missingness(data_imputed)
  peptides_to_impute <- names(missingness[missingness <= miss])
  
  if (length(peptides_to_impute) > 0) {
    start.time <- Sys.time()
    tmp <- impute.matrix(data_imputed[peptides_to_impute, ], method = "knn")
    end.time <- Sys.time()
    cat("Finished imputing all remaining missing values\n")
    print(end.time - start.time)
    data_imputed[match(rownames(tmp), rownames(data_imputed)), match(colnames(tmp), colnames(data_imputed))] <- tmp
  }
  
  df <- melt(data_imputed)
  colnames(df) <- c("peptide_id", "shortname", "intensity_by_group_imputed")
  obj$peptides$intensity_by_group_imputed <- NULL
  obj$peptides <- merge(obj$peptides, df, all = T)
  obj$peptides$sample_id <- obj$samples$sample_id[match(obj$peptides$shortname, obj$samples$shortname)]
  prot_df <- unique(obj$peptides[!is.na(obj$peptides$protein_id), c("peptide_id", "protein_id")])
  obj$peptides$protein_id <- prot_df$protein_id[match(obj$peptides$peptide_id, prot_df$peptide_id)]
  obj$peptides$batch <- obj$samples$ms_batch[match(obj$peptides$shortname, obj$samples$shortname)]
  obj$peptides$sample_type <- obj$samples$sample_type[match(obj$peptides$shortname, obj$samples$shortname)]
  
  # Plot distributions of samples 
  for (st in unique(obj$peptides$sample_type)) {
    tib_plot <- obj$peptides[obj$peptides$sample_type %in% st, ]
    # plot limits
    print(ggplot(tib_plot, aes_string(x = "intensity_by_group_imputed", labels = "sample_id", color = "batch")) +
            geom_line(stat = "density", adjust = 1, bw = "sj", na.rm = T, alpha = 0.33, linewidth = .75) +
            # scale_linetype_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "solid", "TRUE" = "dashed")) +
            xlim(abs(quantile(tib_plot$intensity_by_group_imputed, probs = c(.005, .995), na.rm = T))) +
            labs(x = "log2(imputed_intensity)", y = "Intensity density", title = sprintf("Imputed intensity missingness <=%s for sample type %s", miss, st), colour = "Sample batch") +
            theme_bw())
    print(ggplot(tib_plot, aes_string(x = "intensity_by_group", labels = "sample_id", color = "batch")) +
            geom_line(stat = "density", adjust = 1, bw = "sj", na.rm = T, alpha = 0.33, linewidth = .75) +
            # scale_linetype_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "solid", "TRUE" = "dashed")) +
            xlim(abs(quantile(tib_plot$intensity_by_group, probs = c(.005, .995), na.rm = T))) +
            labs(x = "log2(intensity)", y = "Intensity density", title = sprintf("Intensity missingness <=%s for sample type %s", miss, st), colour = "Sample batch") +
            theme_bw())
  }
}
```

What can be seen from the distribution plots at 34% compared to 40% missingness, the distributions seem fairly similar, so it is sensible to allow for a higher missingness in order to keep more imputed peptides.

```{r Final Global Imputation (≤40% missingness)}
obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])
mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, peptide_id ~ shortname, col = "intensity_by_group_imputed")
data_imputed <- mat
dataset$peptides$intensity_by_group_imputed <- NULL

missingness <- get_missingness(data_imputed)
peptides_to_impute <- names(missingness[missingness <= 40])

if (length(peptides_to_impute) > 0) {
  start.time <- Sys.time()
  tmp <- impute.matrix(data_imputed[peptides_to_impute, ], method = "knn")
  end.time <- Sys.time()
  cat("Finished imputing all peptides with <=40% missingness\n")
  print(end.time - start.time)
  data_imputed[match(rownames(tmp), rownames(data_imputed)), match(colnames(tmp), colnames(data_imputed))] <- tmp
}

df <- melt(data_imputed)
colnames(df) <- c("peptide_id", "shortname", "intensity_by_group_imputed")
dataset$peptides$intensity_by_group_imputed <- NULL
dataset$peptides <- merge(dataset$peptides, df, all = T)

percNA_trace <- as.data.frame(rbind(percNA_trace, c("all", 100 * sum(is.na(data_imputed)) / length(data_imputed))))
print(percNA_trace)
percNA_trace$percNA <- as.numeric(percNA_trace$percNA)
percNA_trace$order <- 1:nrow(percNA_trace)

ggplot(percNA_trace, aes(x=order, y=percNA, label=round(percNA,2))) + geom_line(color="red") + geom_point() + geom_text(hjust=0, vjust=0)
```

```{r Re-normalize imputed data}
# Remove peptides with missingness over 40%
dataset_filt <- remove_exclude_peps(dataset, names(get_missingness(data_imputed)[get_missingness(data_imputed)>40]))
dataset_filt$samples$group <- paste(dataset_filt$samples$sample_type, dataset_filt$samples$analysis_plate96, sep="_")
dataset_filt$peptides$intensity <- dataset_filt$peptides$intensity_by_group_imputed
dataset_filt$peptides$intensity_by_group <- dataset_filt$peptides$intensity_by_group_imputed <- NULL

# Imputation resulted in some rows with NAs; merge the peptide and sample information back into the data 
dataset_filt$peptides$isdecoy <- FALSE
dataset_filt$peptides$detect <- TRUE
## Peptide info
tmp <- unique(dataset_filt$peptides[!is.na(dataset_filt$peptides$sequence_modified), c("peptide_id", "protein_id", "sequence_plain", "sequence_modified")])
dataset_filt$peptides$protein_id <- dataset_filt$peptides$sequence_modified <- dataset_filt$peptides$sequence_plain <- NULL
dataset_filt$peptides <- merge(tmp, dataset_filt$peptides)
## Sample info
tmp <- unique(dataset_filt$peptides[!is.na(dataset_filt$peptides$sample_id), c("shortname", "sample_id")])
dataset_filt$peptides$sample_id <- NULL
dataset_filt$peptides <- merge(tmp, dataset_filt$peptides)

# Remove dt_pep_group and groups sections in dataset, and set them again
dataset_filt$dt_pep_group <- dataset_filt$groups <- NULL
dataset_filt <- cache_filtering_data_noCoV(dataset_filt)
# Normalize data
cat("Normalising imputed data\n")
dataset_filt <- filter_dataset(
  dataset = dataset_filt,
  filter_min_detect = 3, # each peptide must have a good confidence score in at least N samples per group
  filter_min_quant = 3, # similarly, the number of reps where the peptide must have a quantitative value
  by_group = T, all_group = F, by_contrast = F,
  rollup_algorithm = rollup_algorithm, norm_algorithm = c("loess", "modebetween_protein")
) # loess calls the cyclic loess function normalizeCyclicLoess from limma (recommended by Vadim), and the modebetween_protein scales between all pairwise sample groups on a protein level, such that the log-fold-change mode is zero

# Create directory for QC results
outDir <- file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "3_3_imputedAll")
dir.create(outDir, showWarnings = F, recursive = T)
saveRDS(object = dataset_filt, file = file.path(outDir, "impute_all.Rdata"))
```

## Batch effect correction

Although the PCAs do not show a strong batch effect, the qualitative centres did show minor distances between each other, so it may be worthwhile to see whether a batch correction changes the quality and PCAs to a large extent. Furthermore, the other technical aspect that showed some differences are the plate numbers, where qualitative centres of plates 8 and 4 seem quite different from other plates, which is why it may be worthwhile to correct for the batch effect based on the plate numbers.

```{r plot PCA after batch correction}
dataset <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "3_3_imputedAll", "impute_all.Rdata"))
obj <- remove_exclude_samps(dataset, dataset$samples$sample_id[dataset$samples$exclude])
obj <- remove_exclude_samps(obj, obj$samples$sample_id[obj$samples$sample_type %in% c("MS.QC", "SP.QC")])

obj$peptides <- remove_batch_effect(obj, batch = "group", col = "intensity_by_group")
outDir <- file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "4_batchCorrected")
dir.create(outDir, showWarnings = F, recursive = T)

qc_df_batchCorr <- qc_msdap_figures(obj, outDir, batch = "group", type = "sample_type", intensity = "intensity_by_group")

cat("Calculating PCA for plate-corrected data\n")
obj$samples$ms_batch_n <- as.numeric(gsub("b", "", obj$samples$ms_batch))
obj$samples$analysis_plate96_n <- as.numeric(gsub("P", "", obj$samples$analysis_plate96))

mat <- dfToMat(obj$peptides, peptide_id ~ sample_id, col = "intensity_by_group")

res <- pca_msdap_res(dataset = obj, impute = "ppca", features = "peptides", intensity = "intensity_by_group", quanti_vars = c("detected_peptides", "detected_proteins", "ms_batch_n", "analysis_plate96_n"), quali_vars = c("analysis_plate96", "ms_batch"), calc.nPCs = 15)
plot.nPCs <- pca_optimal(res$res.pca)

dir.create(file.path(outDir, "PCA"), showWarnings = F, recursive = T)
pca_msdap_figures(res.pca = res$res.pca, outDir = file.path(outDir, "PCA"), type = "analysis_plate96", calc.nPCs = res$calc.nPCs, plot.nPCs = plot.nPCs)
```

Since the batch removal has worked so well for the biological data, it is implemented on the entire dataset.

```{r Batch correction dataset}
dataset$peptides <- remove_batch_effect(dataset, batch = "group", col = "intensity_by_group")
outDir <- file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "4_batchCorrected")
saveRDS(object = dataset, file = file.path(outDir, "batch_corrected.Rdata"))
```

# Save data

For the clients, they require 3 different matrices:

1.  [Precursor matrix]{.underline} (generated by `final_output` function)

2.  [Protein matrix, without isoform information and proteotypic peptides]{.underline} - matrix for proteotypic peptides and no isoform information

    1.  summarize intensities for proteins, not isoforms (remove "-" and trailing numbers from protein IDs first, then rollup precursor intensities into proteins), and then keep proteins with proteotypic peptides only (remove entries where protein ID contains ";")

3.  [Protein matrix, with isoform information and proteotypic peptides only]{.underline} - protein matrix for proteotypic peptides and keeping isoform information

    1.  summarize to protein level without adjusting the protein IDs (isoforms are kept in tact) and keep proteins with proteotypic peptides only

Each of the matrices should be imputed completely.

```{r save data}
dataset <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "4_batchCorrected", "batch_corrected.Rdata"))
outDir <- file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc")
# Write out metadata file
write.xlsx(x = dataset$samples, file = file.path(outDir, "Metadata.xlsx"))

# Write out results
final_output(dataset = dataset, outDir = outDir, dataFile = "final_dataset.Rdata", rollup_algorithm = rollup_algorithm)
write.xlsx(overall_stats, file.path(outDir, "overall_statistics.xlsx"), rowNames = TRUE, overwrite = T)
```

```{r Generate output requested by client}
dataset <- readRDS(file.path(inDir, "05_DataAnalysis", "02_Rawdata", "preProc", "4_batchCorrected", "batch_corrected.Rdata"))
df <- merge(dataset$peptides %>% dplyr::select(peptide_id, protein_id, sample_id, intensity = intensity_by_group), dataset$proteins[,c("protein_id", "gene_symbols_or_id")])
protein_ids <- unique(df[,c("protein_id", "gene_symbols_or_id")])
# Protein IDs without isoform info
protein_ids$protein_id_noIso <- sapply(1:nrow(protein_ids), function(i){
  if(grepl("-", protein_ids$protein_id[i])){
    if(grepl(";", protein_ids$protein_id[i])){
      paste(unique(gsub("-.*", "", strsplit(protein_ids$protein_id[i], split = ";")[[1]])), collapse=";")
    }else{
      gsub("-*", "", protein_ids$protein_id[i])
    }
  }else{
    protein_ids$protein_id[i]
  }
})
df <- merge(df, protein_ids)

# Rollup different proteins/genes
## Proteins
tmp <- df[,c("peptide_id", "protein_id", "sample_id", "intensity")]
prot_rollup <- rollup_pep2prot(tmp, rollup_algorithm = rollup_algorithm, intensity_is_log2 = T, return_as_matrix = T)
prot_rollup <- merge(unique(df[,c("protein_id", "gene_symbols_or_id")]), prot_rollup, by.x="protein_id", by.y = "row.names")
write.xlsx(prot_rollup, file.path(outDir, "Protein_rollup_intensities.xlsx"), rowNames = TRUE, overwrite = T)
## Proteins without isoform information
tmp <- df[,c("peptide_id", "protein_id_noIso", "sample_id", "intensity")]
colnames(tmp) <- c("peptide_id", "protein_id", "sample_id", "intensity")
prot_noIso_rollup <- rollup_pep2prot(tmp, rollup_algorithm = rollup_algorithm, intensity_is_log2 = T, return_as_matrix = T)
prot_noIso_rollup <- merge(unique(df[,c("protein_id_noIso", "gene_symbols_or_id")]), prot_noIso_rollup, by.x="protein_id_noIso", by.y = "row.names")
write.xlsx(prot_noIso_rollup, file.path(outDir, "Protein_noIso_intensities.xlsx"), rowNames = TRUE, overwrite = T)
## Genes
tmp <- df[,c("peptide_id", "gene_symbols_or_id", "sample_id", "intensity")]
colnames(tmp) <- c("peptide_id", "protein_id", "sample_id", "intensity")
gene_rollup <- rollup_pep2prot(tmp, rollup_algorithm = rollup_algorithm, intensity_is_log2 = T, return_as_matrix = T)
write.xlsx(gene_rollup, file.path(outDir, "Gene_rollup_intensities.xlsx"), rowNames = TRUE, overwrite = T)
```
